findings.description: The agent id format `<name>-agent-1` is defined three times: world.py (`Principal(name, email, f"{name}-agent-1", clone)`), agents.py (`self.agent_id = f"{spec.name}-agent-1"`), and collision.py, which re-derives it as `f"{p.name}-agent-1"` for the report instead of reading `agent.agent_id` from the ScriptedAgent it just created. blocked.py does read `s.agent.agent_id`. A change to the format in one place silently diverges the report from the world/agent.

findings.description: runner.run only catches ScenarioError around `scenario.run(ctx)`. `render()` runs outside that inner try, so a ScenarioError message that happens to contain a 40-hex commit id (git stderr often does) makes `render` raise ReportError, which escapes as an uncaught traceback with no report printed. Likewise a malformed `scenario.yaml` raises yaml.YAMLError out of `load_fixture` before any mapping to exit 64/1. Both end up as exit 1 via the interpreter, which matches the contract's code but not its 'A report carrying a non-null error is printed when possible' intent.
findings.existing_code: text = render(report, forbidden_paths=[v for v, _ in scrub])
findings.resolution: On ReportError, fall back to rendering `new_report(scenario_id, error="report rejected: <reason>")` with exit 1; wrap `yaml.safe_load` in load_fixture to raise UsageError.

findings.description: test_no_probe_is_registered_at_import_time pops `mpsim.probes` from sys.modules and re-imports it. importlib then rebinds the package attribute `mpsim.probes` to the fresh module and the `finally` restores only sys.modules, so for the rest of the session `mpsim.probes` (attribute access) and `sys.modules['mpsim.probes']` are different objects with different `REGISTRY` and `ProbeResult` classes. Nothing currently breaks because every consumer bound the original at import, but any later `from mpsim import probes` evaluated at runtime sees the stale module. Separately, once ri-06 adds `from mpsim.probes import requirement_collision`, the re-import finds that submodule cached, its module-level `register()` does not re-run, and `fresh.REGISTRY == {}` passes trivially, so the test no longer tests what its name claims.
findings.resolution: Assert in a subprocess (`python -c 'import mpsim.probes as p; assert p.REGISTRY == {}'` with the harness root on sys.path) so no in-process module state leaks, and note that ri-06 must retire or invert this test.
